outcome: No accepted proof or counterexample of the Hodge conjecture for general smooth projective varieties has appeared since 26 January 2024. The main event is OpenAI's 6 October 2026 release of a manuscript claiming the rational Hodge conjecture for all complex CM abelian varieties and their products; by 12 October 2026 I found no written verification of that argument, and two of its sister manuscripts from the same release were withdrawn for a sign error.
problem_asks: Statement as given (Wikipedia, January 2024 wording): 'Let X be a non-singular complex projective manifold. Then every Hodge class on X is a linear combination with rational coefficients of the cohomology classes of complex subvarieties of X.' Parts: (a) every non-singular complex projective variety X, in every dimension; (b) every Hodge class in the rational cohomology of X, in every degree (equivalently every codimension k, the (k,k)-classes); (c) the conclusion is a linear combination with rational coefficients (the integral version is not what is asked); (d) the classes are realised by classes of complex subvarieties (algebraic cycles). The bullet asks for all of (a) to (d) at once, not for a special class such as abelian varieties, a fixed dimension or a fixed codimension.

events.what_happened: On 6 Oct 2026 OpenAI published, in the openai/math GitHub repository, a release of 722 manuscripts in 372 result families, which its README says contains manuscripts and proof artifacts 'produced by an internal OpenAI model'. One manuscript, 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties' (dated 30 Sep 2026 on its own README and folder; the only author listed is 'OpenAI'), has an abstract that reads 'We prove the rational Hodge conjecture for complex abelian varieties with complex multiplication: every rational Hodge class on such a variety is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes' (as rendered by the fetch tool). Its Theorem 1 covers every finite product of CM abelian varieties in every codimension. The abstract also lists consequences: the generalized Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields, and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic, the last two via Milne's theorems. That Altman singled this result out as one of four highlights, and that he said the claims were not yet confirmed by outside mathematicians, comes from secondary reports only (officechai, kingy.ai); openai.com returned HTTP 403 and I could not open the post.
events.revisions: Manuscript dated 30 Sep 2026 (README and folder name). The repository's first commit ('Initial commit', adc7f12) is dated 6 Oct 2026, the release date given by the catalogue and by most outlets; one outlet dates the GitHub upload to 7 Oct. Later commits on 8 Oct 2026 ('Update manuscripts and Lean formalizations', 3014888). history.md has one entry, dated 7 Oct 2026, which withdraws three other manuscripts and repairs 14; it does not list this manuscript as withdrawn or as dependent on a withdrawn one. I found no earlier public version.
events.delivers: The rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and every codimension, and (Theorem 1) for every finite product of CM abelian varieties. Restricted to CM abelian varieties and their products. The listed consequences (Tate for abelian varieties over finite fields; Hodge standard conjecture in arbitrary characteristic; generalized Hodge for CM abelian varieties) are asserted through cited results (Milne 1999 and 2002 with addenda, Abdulali 2005, Hazama); I did not check those inferences.
events.remains: The rational Hodge conjecture for abelian varieties that are not of CM type, and for all other non-singular complex projective varieties, which is the full problem as stated. The integral version is not addressed. The consequences listed above are asserted, not separately established by me.
events.time_since_posted: 6 days to 12 Oct 2026 (manuscript dated 30 Sep, so 12 days)
events.directly_checkable: Not a finite object; it is a proof. The steps a specialist could check directly are the four-factor switch theorem (Theorem 'switch' and Prop 'switch-reduction' in section 06), the surface criterion (Prop 3.1 in section 03, which concludes that 'the line ... is algebraic'), and the finite-family extraction corollary. I have not checked any of them.
events.doubts: (1) Sister manuscripts in the same release were withdrawn for a sign error in a stabilization-trace cancellation argument (see the split-eightfold event and the K3 events). This manuscript was not withdrawn, and the withdrawal notices and history.md do not list it as dependent. Sources disagree on whether it is affected: KuCoin (MarsBit, citing Machine Heart) says the core CM claim 'remains intact', while kingy.ai says it 'requires its own scrutiny'. I read sections 01 (introduction), 03, 05c, 06 and 07 of its LaTeX. The introduction says Milne's and Deligne-Andre's reduction expresses CM Hodge classes through divisor and split Weil classes, and it cites Markman's sixfold work. Section 06 invokes only internal results (Theorem switch, Proposition switch-reduction, Corollaries finite-family-extraction and surface-span) and cites no withdrawn manuscript, no stabilization-trace construction and no Weil-class algebraicity result in dimension 8. Sections 02, 04, 05a, 05b and 05b-satake-frobenius were not read, and the PDF itself was not extractable. (2) The README lists the CM Hodge result among 'Exceptions to this fixed procedure'; what the exception consisted of is not stated in the pages I could read. (3) The manuscript cites an OpenAI companion 'OpenAIMilneRationality2026' (Corollary 3.4) that I did not find in the repository's preprint listing. (4) Lean: no formalization is listed for it (catalogue, via a secondary summary); the README says 'Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations' and that some unformalized results 'could have issues'. (5) No human author is named, and the release is described as not yet peer reviewed. (6) An anonymous comment on Terence Tao's blog dated 6 Oct 2026 says OpenAI proved this result; it is not a verification and I give it no weight.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction: it asserts that the rational Hodge conjecture holds for the stated class, and it exhibits no counterexample. It settles the problem only for CM abelian varieties and their products, and leaves the full statement untouched.

events.what_happened: 'Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds' (folder dated 18 Sep 2026; author OpenAI) claimed algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds, which are 8-dimensional varieties. It was withdrawn with a notice that its proof 'contains a sign error in the stabilization-trace argument used to obtain negative double points'. The notice says the paper assigns each reverse stabilization trace sign +1 where the count requires -1, so that I_new = I(f1) - m = -2m, not 0; the Eliashberg-Murphy cancellation theorem then has an unmet hypothesis and the subsequent surgery and embedded-brane construction is unsupported. The notice says the paper 'does not establish its claimed algebraicity theorem' and that the withdrawal 'concerns the proof; it does not assert that the mathematical statement is false.'
events.revisions: Manuscript folder dated 18 Sep 2026. Notice: 'Withdrawn on October 6, 2026'. history.md dates the withdrawal to 7 Oct 2026 and says the sign error 'invalidates a stabilization-trace cancellation argument and the construction used by two dependent papers'. The date given is the first public appearance I could establish (6 Oct).
events.delivers: Withdrawn. Claimed algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds, which would have settled that Hodge-class question in dimension 8. Per the notice, the proof does not establish it, so it delivers nothing currently.
events.remains: Algebraicity of split Weil classes on abelian eightfolds, which the withdrawal leaves unproved. I found no other source that proves it, and the 2025 Markman results cover sixfolds and fourfolds.
events.directly_checkable: The disputed step is a sign convention for reverse stabilization traces and the resulting double-point count. Two outside checks (below) examine it; neither is a verification of the theorem.
events.doubts: Outside checks of the sign convention. (a) github.com/ityonemo/openai-wiles, a 2b4m formalisation of the two sign chains: 'The -right chain is that paragraph, machine-checked' ... 'Neither chain decides which convention is right' ... 'this sign is the hinge'; it also says 'Sections 4-11's symplectic topology is not verified'. (b) github.com/mrnathanhumphrey-droid/openai-split-eightfold-gap, a Python check: 'In every even dimension n = 2..14, the forward-trace double point is not orientably surgerable', with the caveat 'It does not show that the paper's theorem is false.' A secondary report (AIWeekly) says a post by Elliot Glazer reports that an automated checker found the paper 'seems to be flawed'; I did not open that post. The authors' own withdrawal concurs that the proof fails as written.

events.what_happened: Ningyi Li, 'The Tate conjecture for powers of abelian fourfolds and the Hodge conjecture for powers of CM fourfolds', arXiv:2609.27916, v1 submitted 10 Sep 2026. The abstract claims the Tate conjecture in every codimension on every power of an abelian variety of dimension at most four over a finite field, and 'the Hodge conjecture for every power of a complex CM abelian fourfold'. v2 (8 Oct 2026) is marked withdrawn 'following a reassessment of the paper's contribution in light of recent work on the Hodge and Tate conjectures for abelian varieties'.
events.revisions: v1 10 Sep 2026 (45 KB); v2 8 Oct 2026 (1 KB), withdrawn.
events.delivers: Per the v1 abstract: Hodge for every power of a complex CM abelian fourfold (dimension four only, all powers); Tate for powers of abelian varieties of dimension at most four over finite fields in the cases stated. The Hodge part overlaps the dimension-four cases of the OpenAI CM claim. Withdrawn.
events.remains: Withdrawn, so nothing is established by this entry; the Hodge statement for CM abelian varieties of dimension five and above is outside the abstract's claim.

events.what_happened: Eyal Markman, 'Cycles on abelian 2n-folds of Weil type from secant sheaves on abelian n-folds', arXiv:2502.03415. The abstract states that 'the Weil classes are algebraic for all abelian sixfolds of Weil type of discriminant -1', for all imaginary quadratic fields, and that 'the algebraicity of the Weil classes follows for all abelian fourfolds of Weil type', which the abstract says gives the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds. Tao's blog guest posts (Totaro, 11 Sep 2026; Voisin, 12 Sep 2026) describe the result as proving the Hodge conjecture for abelian varieties of dimension 4 and 5, via the Moonen-Zarhin reduction to Weil type.
events.revisions: v1 5 Feb 2025 (2.7 MB); v2 8 Jun 2025 ('96 pages, 1 figure. Improved notation consistency and added a table of notation as Section 12. Section 8.1 is new').
events.delivers: Algebraicity of the Weil classes on abelian sixfolds of Weil type with discriminant -1 (all imaginary quadratic fields), hence on all abelian fourfolds of Weil type by Schoen's degeneration, hence the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds of Weil type (per the abstract). Restricted to Weil type; discriminant -1 for sixfolds.
events.remains: Weil classes on abelian sixfolds of Weil type with other discriminants; Hodge for abelian varieties of dimension six and higher in general; the Hodge conjecture for all abelian varieties (which Moonen and Zarhin reduce to the Weil-type case, per the Totaro post); all non-abelian varieties.

events.what_happened: Amir Mostaed, 'McMullen's Curve, the Weil Locus, and the Hodge Conjecture for Abelian Sixfolds', arXiv:2603.20268, submitted 14 Mar 2026. The abstract studies McMullen's curve in a Hilbert modular sixfold and its intersection with the Weil locus. It proves that the intersection is finite, possibly empty, and that every point is a CM point, reduces non-emptiness for two discriminants to explicit equations at a prime, and says the Hodge-Weil classes at intersection points are 'inaccessible to all existing algebraicity theorems'. It aims to 'isolate the remaining open steps toward a new case of the Hodge conjecture for abelian sixfolds'.
events.revisions: One version (v1, 14 Mar 2026, 49 KB, 43 pages).
events.delivers: Structural results on the intersection (finite, CM points) and a reduction of non-emptiness to finite computations for two discriminants. It does not prove that any Hodge class is algebraic.
events.remains: Algebraicity of the Hodge-Weil classes at the intersection points, which the abstract presents as open.
events.direction: Not a resolution in either direction; it isolates open steps toward a case of the conjecture.

The abstract says the paper 'gives another proof of the Hodge conjecture for the general abelian fourfold of Weil type with trivial discriminant', by mapping the fourfolds to a hyper-Kahler sixfold of K3^[3] type and showing that the pullback of the second Chern class of the sixfold's tangent bundle is an algebraic codimension-two class that is not an intersection of divisor classes.
events.revisions: One version (v1, 20 Jul 2026, 53 KB).

events.what_happened: Ananyo Dan and Inder Kaur, 'Hodge Conjecture via Singular Varieties', arXiv:2509.25273, submitted 28 Sep 2025, superseding arXiv:2301.01005. The paper studies the cohomological and Jannsen's homological Hodge conjecture for singular varieties. It proves that odd-dimensional hypersurfaces with A_n singularities satisfy both versions, and notes that their smooth resolutions then satisfy the classical Hodge conjecture, giving new smooth examples.
events.revisions: One version (v1, 28 Sep 2025, 67 KB); supersedes arXiv:2301.01005.
events.delivers: For odd-dimensional hypersurfaces with A_n singularities: the singular versions of the Hodge conjecture, and as a consequence the classical Hodge conjecture for their smooth resolutions. The singular versions are a different question; the classical consequence is the part that bears on this bullet, and only for that restricted class.
events.remains: Hypersurfaces with other singularities; smooth varieties in general.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction for a restricted class of smooth examples, and for a singular variant.

events.what_happened: Badre Mounda, 'Constructive Proof of the Hodge Conjecture for K3 Surfaces via Nodal Degenerations', arXiv:2507.18999, v1 25 Jul 2025 (only version). The abstract claims 'a constructive proof of the Hodge conjecture for complex K3 surfaces' for rational (1,1)-classes, through a one-parameter family of quartic K3s with at most ten nodes, and an equivariant extension for (2,2)-classes on Calabi-Yau threefolds.
events.revisions: One version (v1, 25 Jul 2025, 15 KB).
events.delivers: For K3 surfaces, the (1,1)-classes case, by a constructive method. That case is classical: the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem gives every integral (1,1)-class on a Kahler manifold as a divisor class, so the new content is the construction, not the statement. The (2,2) extension on Calabi-Yau threefolds is the claimed new part; I did not evaluate it.
events.remains: The Hodge conjecture in higher codimension and for other varieties; the (2,2) claim is only as strong as its proof, which I did not check.
events.doubts: The (1,1) case for surfaces is covered by the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem (Wikipedia, 'Lefschetz theorem on (1,1)-classes', which says that theorem holds for all compact Kahler manifolds); the abstract does not mention that theorem.
events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction for a classical case, with a claimed construction.

events.what_happened: Dongzhe Zheng, arXiv:2506.17754 (single author; listed math.GM). The abstract claims that 'this dimension matching result is sufficient to verify the (1,1)-type Hodge conjecture' for 5-dimensional Calabi-Yau manifolds with h^{1,1} = 56 carrying E7 group constraints, by a non-constructive argument. The arXiv abstract page gives the title 'Exceptional Symmetry as a Source of Algebraic Cycles: Non-Constructive Methods for the Hodge Conjecture for a Special Class of Calabi-Yau 5-Folds'; the v1 title as quoted by a search summary was 'A Proof of the Hodge Conjecture for a Special Class of Calabi-Yau 5-Folds via Exceptional Group Constraints'.
events.revisions: v1 21 Jun 2025 (37 KB); v2 24 Jun 2025 marked '(withdrawn)', no reason given; v3 3 Jul 2025 (37 KB), current.
events.delivers: The (1,1)-type Hodge conjecture for one class of Calabi-Yau 5-folds. Codimension one.
events.remains: Codimensions two and higher, and all other varieties. The codimension-one case for all smooth projective varieties is already a theorem (Lefschetz (1,1)), so the claim is a special case of a known result as stated.
events.doubts: The codimension-one (1,1) case is a special case of the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem (Wikipedia, 'Lefschetz theorem on (1,1)-classes'), and the abstract-level read does not mention that theorem. The v2 withdrawal is not explained. Single author; no journal or expert engagement found.

withdrawn.what: v2 (24 Jun 2025) marked withdrawn; v3 (3 Jul 2025) is the current version.

events.direction: Cuts in the conjectured direction for a codimension-one case of a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Karim Mansour (submitter listed as Karem Ahmed Mansour Abdelgalil), 'A Deformation Theoretic Reduction of the Hodge Conjecture via Derived Categories and Complete Intersections', arXiv:2507.09934. The abstract proposes 'a geometric and categorical approach to the Hodge Conjecture for all smooth projective complex varieties', claims to 'prove the conjecture unconditionally in the complete intersection case using derived category methods', and reduces the general case by deformation to 'the algebraicity of limits', which the abstract says 'remains an assumption'. v2 (14 Aug 2025) is marked withdrawn with the comment 'Error in argument'.
events.revisions: v1 14 Jul 2025 (10 KB); v2 14 Aug 2025 (1 KB), withdrawn by the submitter.
events.delivers: Claimed in v1: the Hodge conjecture for smooth complete intersections, by derived-category methods. Withdrawn, so this entry establishes nothing.
events.remains: Complete intersections: unproved per the withdrawal. General case: reduced to algebraicity of limits, which the abstract treats as an assumption.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the submitter with the comment 'Error in argument'; the withdrawal does not say which argument failed.

withdrawn.what: v2 (14 Aug 2025) withdrawn by the submitter; comment 'Error in argument'.

events.direction: Would prove the conjectured statement for complete intersections, and reduce the general case to an assumption. Withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Johann Bouali, 'Degeneration of families of projective hypersurfaces and Hodge conjecture', arXiv:2401.03465. The abstract says: 'We prove by induction on dimension the Hodge conjecture for smooth complex projective varieties.' The comments field reads 'arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2312.09268'. No journal reference is listed. Thirteen versions exist.
events.delivers: Claims the full conjecture: the Hodge conjecture for all smooth complex projective varieties, by induction on dimension.
events.remains: Nothing, on the author's claim. I did not read the full text, so I cannot say what the induction rests on.
events.time_since_posted: about 2 years 9 months since v1; about 2 years since v13
events.direction: Claims the conjectured statement in full; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Yoshinori Shimizu, 'Proof of the Hodge Conjecture', Zenodo record 16885094, published 16 Aug 2025 (page also shows 'Modified June 16, 2026'), version 1.0a, labelled a working draft that 'has not yet been finalized for publication'. The description says 'In this paper we prove the Rational Hodge Conjecture, namely that for every smooth complex projective variety'.
events.revisions: Version 1.0a; the attached PDF is labelled v1.1; page modified 16 Jun 2026.
events.delivers: Claims the full rational conjecture for every smooth complex projective variety.
events.remains: Nothing, on the author's claim.
events.doubts: Self-published working draft on Zenodo, a repository that does not review content; the page itself says it has not been finalized for publication.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured statement in full; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Zenodo record 15335318, 'Proof of Hodge's conjecture', by 이, 상운 (listed as such on the page), published 4 May 2025, labelled preprint, open access. The record has no description or abstract; the title is the only content.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Claims a proof of the Hodge conjecture by title only. The record gives no scope, so nothing about its scope can be read.
events.remains: Not determinable from the record.
events.doubts: The record contains no content to assess; it is self-posted on a non-reviewing repository.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured statement; scope unknown.

events.what_happened: Zenodo record 15489331, 'Proof of Hodge's Conjecture', by 이, 상운, published 22 May 2025, preprint, open access. No description or abstract on the record.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Claims a proof of the Hodge conjecture by title only. Scope not readable from the record.
events.remains: Not determinable from the record.
events.doubts: The record contains no content to assess; self-posted on a non-reviewing repository. Probably the same author as the 4 May 2025 record, but the record does not link them.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured statement; scope unknown.

events.what_happened: Myo Oo, 'E8-Holographic Resolution of the Hodge Conjecture', Zenodo record 18527717, published 8 Feb 2026, version 1, open access. The description opens by describing the conjecture and proposes a resolution within an 'E8-Holographic Framework' that treats cohomology as emerging from a discrete 8-dimensional root lattice. The page says verification consists of the author's own computational script.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Claims a resolution of the full conjecture, per the description. No scope narrower than the statement is given.
events.remains: Nothing, on the author's claim.
events.directly_checkable: The author's own computational script, which the page mentions; I did not open it.
events.doubts: Self-posted record on a non-reviewing repository; the only verification named is the author's own script.
events.direction: Claims the conjectured statement in full; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Michael K. Brown and Mark E. Walker, 'The Hodge structure on the singularity category of a complex hypersurface', arXiv:2407.09988. The abstract identifies the noncommutative Hodge structure on the periodic cyclic homology of a singularity category with the classical Hodge structure on the primitive cohomology of the associated projective hypersurface, and 'the Hodge conjecture for the projective hypersurface is equivalent to a dg-categorical analogue of the Hodge conjecture for the singularity category'.
events.revisions: v1 13 Jul 2024 (35 KB); v2 15 Aug 2025 (36 KB), current. A search summary says it was published in Annals of K-theory in 2025; I did not confirm that from the arXiv page.
events.delivers: An equivalence: the Hodge conjecture for projective hypersurfaces is equivalent to a dg-categorical analogue for the singularity category. No case of the conjecture is settled.
events.remains: Everything: the equivalence transfers the question to another formulation.
events.direction: A reformulation, neither way.

events.what_happened: Mauro Varesco, 'The Hodge conjecture for powers of K3 surfaces of Picard number 16', arXiv:2203.09778, v1 18 Mar 2022, v3 13 May 2024. The abstract says that if the Kuga-Satake correspondence is algebraic for a family of K3 surfaces of generic Picard number 16, then the Hodge conjecture holds for all powers of any K3 surface in that family. The comments say it is 'to appear on the Michigan Mathematical Journal'.
events.revisions: v1 18 Mar 2022 (24 KB); v2 16 Jun 2022 (27 KB); v3 13 May 2024 (27 KB), current.
events.delivers: Conditional: the Hodge conjecture for all powers of K3 surfaces in a Picard-number-16 family, given algebraicity of the Kuga-Satake correspondence for that family. Unconditional for no case.
events.remains: The Kuga-Satake algebraicity hypothesis, which is the open input.
events.direction: Conditional reduction in the conjectured direction.

events.what_happened: K. H. Kim and F. W. Roush, 'Counterexample to the Hodge Conjecture', arXiv:math/0608265, v1 10 Aug 2006. The abstract constructs a K3 surface whose products are 'candidates for counterexamples'. The v2 comment (22 Aug 2006) states: 'We no longer claim to have disproved the Hodge conjecture.'
events.revisions: v1 10 Aug 2006; v2 22 Aug 2006, withdrawing the disproof claim in the comment.
events.delivers: Nothing: products of the K3 surface are candidates only, and the authors withdraw the claim to have disproved the conjecture.
events.remains: The question stays as it was.
events.doubts: The authors withdrew the counterexample claim in v2.

withdrawn.what: The v2 comment says the authors no longer claim to have disproved the conjecture.

events.direction: Would be a counterexample if the candidates were confirmed; the claim was withdrawn.
events.object: A K3 surface whose transcendental lattice has a self-isomorphism that is not a rational combination of self-isomorphisms preserving cup products up to nonzero multiples; products of this surface are proposed as candidate counterexamples. Not established.

events.what_happened: Renyi Ma, 'A Counter Example To the Hodge Conjecture', arXiv:0808.1402, v1 10 Aug 2008. The abstract says: 'In this paper, we give a simple counter example to the famous Hodge conjecture.' v3 (9 May 2010) is marked withdrawn; v4 (10 Feb 2012) and v5 (22 Jan 2013) followed. The page gives no reason for the withdrawal, and I did not read the body.
events.revisions: v1 10 Aug 2008; v2 22 Sep 2008; v3 9 May 2010 (withdrawn); v4 10 Feb 2012; v5 22 Jan 2013.
events.delivers: Claims a counterexample to the conjecture. The body was not readable from the page, so what the counterexample is cannot be stated.
events.remains: Unknown.
events.doubts: v3 is marked withdrawn; the record shows no reason and no expert response.

withdrawn.what: v3 (9 May 2010) is marked withdrawn; later versions restore the text.

events.direction: Would be a counterexample to the conjecture, if correct; the record does not establish that.
events.object: A counterexample claimed in a short note; the body was not readable, so the object is not described here.

events.what_happened: Philip Engel, Olivier de Gaay Fortman and Stefan Schreieder, 'Matroids and the integral Hodge conjecture for abelian varieties', arXiv:2507.15704. The abstract says the cohomology class of any curve on a very general principally polarised abelian variety of dimension at least 4 is an even multiple of the minimal class, which 'disproves the integral Hodge conjecture for abelian varieties'; it also treats very general cubic threefolds.
events.revisions: v1 21 Jul 2025 (206 KB); v2 7 Aug 2025 (207 KB); v3 27 Mar 2026 (214 KB, 85 pages; Corollary 1.2 improved, Definition 3.2 corrected).
events.delivers: Disproves the integral Hodge conjecture for very general principally polarised abelian varieties of dimension at least 4, and for intermediate Jacobians of very general cubic threefolds. This is a different question from the rational conjecture the bullet asks about, so it neither settles nor moves the rational case.
events.remains: The rational Hodge conjecture is untouched by this result.
events.direction: Refutes the integral version for a class of abelian varieties; the bullet's statement uses rational coefficients, so this cuts against a neighbouring question, not the bullet.

disputes.summary: Whether the CM manuscript is affected by the sign-error withdrawals. KuCoin (MarsBit, citing Machine Heart) says the core CM claim 'remains intact' and that the retraction 'applies to the proofs, not to the mathematical propositions'. kingy.ai says the CM claim 'remains listed and requires its own scrutiny'. The history.md entry lists no CM dependency. No source reads the CM proof's dependencies in full, so this is open.

Withdrawal dates conflict: the K3-products and eightfold notices say 6 Oct 2026; history.md dates the withdrawals 7 Oct 2026; one outlet dates the release to 7 Oct rather than 6 Oct. The repository's first commit is 6 Oct 2026.

Manuscript and Lean counts disagree: 722 manuscripts at release and 719 after withdrawals; Lean coverage given as 300 of 719 (about 42%) by the repository update and Kingy, as 162 of 722 main results by another source, and as 235 of 372 families with Lean documents by Kingy's own count. The README wording is 'Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations'; one secondary source quotes 'many, but not all'.

Altman's statements (that the first, second and fourth highlighted claims have Lean proofs and the Hodge claim does not, and that none is yet confirmed by outside mathematicians) are reported by officechai and kingy.ai. I could not open the OpenAI post or the X post (openai.com returned HTTP 403), so these rest on secondary reporting.
Elliot Glazer's reported post that an automated checker (Astra) found the eightfold paper 'seems to be flawed' is known only from AIWeekly's summary; I did not open the post.

summary: Since 26 January 2024 I found no accepted proof or counterexample of the Hodge conjecture for general smooth projective varieties. The events are restricted cases, unrestricted claims that nobody has engaged with, withdrawn claims, and one large AI-linked claim. The AI-linked claim is OpenAI's manuscript 'The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties', released with 721 others on 6 Oct 2026 (the manuscript itself is dated 30 Sep 2026; the repository's first commit is dated 6 Oct). I read the manuscript's abstract and the LaTeX of five of its ten sections (introduction, surface, CM types, assembly, consequences), the repository README (which states that the vast majority of results used an unreleased internal OpenAI model and names this CM result as an exception to that fixed procedure), the history.md changelog, and the commit log. The PDF itself was not extractable. Secondary reports say Altman described the claims as unconfirmed by outside mathematicians and say the Hodge result has no Lean proof; the catalogue summary I saw lists no formalization for it. By 12 October 2026 I found no written verification of the CM argument. The named commentary I found (Sutherland, Litt, Wood, Townsend, Buckmaster, Tao, the Association for Human Mathematics, and the Institute for Advanced Study advisory group, which says it is 'up to the mathematical community' to assess) concerns the release, its method and the withdrawals, not the CM proof itself. Terence Tao's blog hosts two September 2026 guest posts on the Hodge conjecture (Totaro on Markman's work, Voisin on its status), neither of which discusses the OpenAI manuscript in its body; an anonymous comment there dated 6 Oct says OpenAI proved the result, and I give it no weight. The close question is dependency on withdrawn work. Three sister manuscripts were withdrawn for a sign error in a stabilization-trace argument in the split-eightfold Weil-class paper, and the K3 notice says the K3 products proof relies on that construction. The CM manuscript was not withdrawn. The sections I read do not cite the eightfold paper or the construction, and section 06 invokes only internal results. But its introduction describes the classical reduction of CM Hodge classes to split Weil classes (Milne's 2020 note, which I read, says exactly that for CM-type abelian varieties), and the withdrawn eightfold theorem is an algebraicity statement for split Weil classes in dimension 8. For a claim covering all CM abelian varieties in every dimension, that is the input one would expect to need. I could not settle this from the sections read, and the reports disagree. Two readings: (a) the CM result stands as a claimed, unverified special case whose argument does not use the withdrawn construction, which the authors' own exception language and the sections read are consistent with; (b) it may inherit an unresolved gap in the split-Weil input without the authors flagging it. Outside the OpenAI release, the restricted-case record since 2024 is real. Markman (Feb 2025) proved algebraicity of Weil classes on sixfolds of discriminant -1 and the Hodge conjecture for abelian fourfolds of Weil type, and Floccari and Fu (2025), Floccari (2025), van Geemen and Rapagnetta (2026), Mostaed (2026), Payne (2026) and Jumagulov (2026, a computer-assisted census for odd-degree Fermat fourfolds up to 199) add cases or reductions; Ningyi Li (Sep 2026) claimed Hodge for powers of CM fourfolds and withdrew on 8 Oct 2026. On the other side, the unrestricted claims since 2024 (Bouali, Jan 2024, thirteen versions, no uptake found; Shimizu, Aug 2025; Oo, Feb 2026; two 2025 Zenodo titles with no content) have no expert engagement I could find, and I did not read Bouali's full text. Zheng (2025) claims the codimension-one case for one class of Calabi-Yau fivefolds, which the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem already gives as a special case of a known result; v2 was withdrawn. Old counterexample claims (Kim and Roush, 2006, withdrawn in substance; Ma, 2008, v3 withdrawn) predate the window. On AI: the Information report via Gizmodo and The Decoder (17 Sep 2026) that OpenAI employees expected a Hodge solution soon rests on a single anonymous source and is not a written argument, so it is described here but not recorded as an event. No Google DeepMind, Anthropic, xAI or Gemini Hodge claim surfaced. For events read only at abstract level, ai.none_found means no system is named in what I read; it is not a full-text finding.
competing_reading: The strongest case for reading the CM manuscript as a real advance: it is a complete argument for an infinite class of abelian varieties in every dimension, beyond the Weil-type cases that Markman, Floccari-Fu and van Geemen-Rapagnetta cover. Its introduction and assembly section cite no withdrawn result, the withdrawal notices say they concern proofs and not propositions, and the notices state that the statements are not asserted false. On that reading, the CM result is a claimed, unverified restricted settlement that stands on its own argument and should be recorded as a case of the conjecture, pending review. Against that, the authors themselves flag the CM result as an exception to their procedure, and the sister eightfold and K3 manuscripts failed on an argument of the same type (a trace/cancellation construction), so the same kind of gap cannot be ruled out in the CM proof without reading the sections I did not read.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A written verification of the CM manuscript by specialists in Hodge theory of abelian varieties and Weil classes, or a Lean formalisation of its main theorem with a statement check. (2) Reading sections 02 (tensors), 04 (theta), 05a (moduli), 05b (Frobenius) and 05b-satake-frobenius of the CM LaTeX for any use of split Weil classes in dimension 8, the stabilization-trace construction, or the withdrawn eightfold theorem; and locating the 'OpenAIMilneRationality2026' companion. (3) An OpenAI notice on the history page saying whether the CM result depends on the withdrawn manuscripts. (4) For the AI question: OpenAI's own account of what the exception to its fixed procedure was for the CM result, which the README does not give. (5) For Bouali, Shimizu, Oo and Zheng: an expert reading or a published refereed version, none of which I found.

incomplete: Gaps, in order of importance. (1) The CM manuscript's PDF was not extractable; I read the LaTeX of sections 01, 03, 05c, 06 and 07 only. Sections 02 (tensors), 04 (theta), 05a (moduli), 05b (Frobenius) and 05b-satake-frobenius, and its bibliography, were not read, so the dependency question is open. The companion 'OpenAIMilneRationality2026' was not located. (2) The OpenAI announcement page (openai.com, HTTP 403) and the X posts were not reachable; the Altman statements, the claim that the Hodge result lacks Lean, and the claimed 'four highlights' come from secondary reports. (3) Full texts of Markman (2502.03415), Mostaed, van Geemen-Rapagnetta, Payne, Jumagulov, Floccari, Floccari-Fu, Dan-Kaur, Mounda, Zheng, Bouali, Shimizu, Oo, Brown-Walker, Varesco, Kim-Roush, Ma and Engel et al. were not read; for those the record reflects the abstract or metadata as rendered by the fetch tool, and ai.none_found is therefore a statement about the pages read. Markman's PDF was not extractable. (4) Journal status of Floccari-Fu and Floccari (JMPA and Geometry and Topology) rests on the authors' arXiv comments; the journal pages were not reachable. (5) Not recorded as events, with reasons: the Lippy Google Doc (could not open), preprints.org 202602.0462 (could not open), the Voisin 2002 analytic counterexample (could not open; a different question), the Atiyah-Hirzebruch and Grothendieck pre-1980 integral and general-form counterexamples (different questions; only Wikipedia-attested), and the Gizmodo/The Information report of 17 Sep 2026 (an anonymous expectation, not a written argument). (6) The Elliot Glazer post reported via AIWeekly was not opened. (7) Quotations from the openai/math README, history.md and the CM manuscript are as rendered by the fetch tool's summariser, not raw text, and should be checked against the repository before use. (8) Dates of the release items use the first public appearance I could establish (the 6 Oct 2026 first commit); whether any manuscript circulated earlier is not established. (9) The Clay Institute has not been checked on any Hodge statement beyond the page fetched.
